It cuts the week to about 20 mi with an 8 mi long run, well down from 31–44, and asks for a professional assessment this week, both in the reply and as a safety flag. It keeps Monday and Friday as rest days, and every run is gated on how the previous one went ("only if Tuesday was clean", "if anything is worse... make it 30"), so the week can be run as written.

It answers the first question directly: keep up gentle easy running as long as it isn't making things worse. The second answer is honest but thin. "I am not the right person" sends Johnny to a physio without giving any warning signs to watch for until then, such as pain that gets worse during a run, swelling, worse stiffness in the morning, pain when hopping, or a pop. The draft also does little for his stated anxiety about losing the block, and says nothing about what this means for the Lakeshore Marathon on 15 November. Those gaps keep it from a 5.

── JOHNNY'S WEEK ──
Johnny is training for a fourth marathon, the Lakeshore Marathon on 15 November, aiming for 3:30 against a best of 3:41. Johnny runs five days a week with Monday and Friday as fixed rest days, and prefers mileage to rise carefully after shin splints in a first marathon block.
Recent weeks: 38, 43, 34, 44 mi
This week: 31 mi over 5 runs.
Pain noted: Thu Right Achilles tight from about mile 2 of the session. Got sharper as I picked up the…; Sat Achilles stiff for the first mile, eased after that. About a 3 out of 10.; Sun No pain while running. Stiff getting out of the car afterwards.
Body: "Right Achilles, just above the heel. Tight and a bit tender to press. No swelling that I can see. It was fine until the tempo."
Feeling: "Anxious. I don't want to throw away the block over this."
Asks: "Should I stop running for a few days, or keep going with easy runs?"
Asks: "How do I know if this is serious?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Johnny: The Achilles is the whole story this week, so we pull volume and intensity back and get a professional eye on it. …
Answers: (1) Neither extreme. Do not try to push through, and do not sit still for a week either — some gentle movement usually helps more than full rest with Achilles stuff, as long as it is not making things worse. (2) I am not the right person to answer that — that is a sports-medicine or physio call, and I would get one on the calendar this week rather than wait and see. …
Safety flag: Get the Achilles looked at this week
